svg.title: CBC results: Hgb 10.8 g/dL, Hct 32% . The client reports mild fatigue but no other symptoms. Normal: hemoglobin 11 g/dL or higher and hematocrit 33% or higher in the first and third trimesters (10.5 g/dL and 32% in the second)
svg.desc: Red blood cell mass rises roughly 30% during pregnancy, but plasma volume expands even more, producing an expected physiologic dilutional anemia rather than a pathologic process like acute blood loss or hemolysis. Rising levels of clotting factors during pregnancy create a hypercoagulable state that can raise venous thromboembolism risk as much as fivefold above the nonpregnant baseline. A twofold or threefold estimate understates the risk increase described in the source.
